newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy on uptrend - MOF's Sakakibara quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy on uptrend - MOF's Sakakibara quoted.

text.p: The Japanese economy is now on an upward trend, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, was quoted by Wednesday's Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper as saying.

Sakakibara told the paper in an interview that Japan's long-term interest rates were at record low levels, reflecting a market view that the economy had been in bad shape for a considerable period of time.

"However, once people realise that the Japanese economy is not that bad, long-term interest rates will rise, causing a plunge in bond prices and thus forcing people who are now buying bonds to incur losses," he said.

"The Japanese economy is now on an upward trend... The upside risk for the economy is now higher than the downside risk. Japanese people themselves must now realise the possibility (of the upside risk)," Sakakibara was quoted as saying.
He said it would be natural for stock prices in Japan to rise as the economy is moving ahead.

"However, Japanese financial institutions are not making full-fledged attempts to buy stocks yet. A vast amount of money is now in Japan, but that money is now being used to buy Japanese bonds and it is flowing out of Japan, causing the depreciation of the yen," he was quoted as saying.
